slides.h1: 22% of India's finance openings sit in Mumbai, and 32 companies hold all of them.
slides.sub: 2,067 finance, risk and compliance roles, read this month from 220+ MNC career pages.
slides.caption:
22% of India's finance openings sit in Mumbai, and 32 companies hold all of them.

Our agents read 220+ MNC career pages this month and pulled close to 23,000 openings. 2,067 of them are finance, risk and compliance roles in India.

slides.sub: roles each, from 32 employers. 453 openings, 21.9% of the country, and the deepest market in it.
slides.caption: Mumbai has 21.9% of India's finance openings, which is 453 roles. They come from 32 employers, 14.2 roles each, the deepest per-employer market in the country. Entry level runs 19.3%, the highest of any big metro.

head: Employer
Openings
slides.note: Career pages of one firm are counted as one employer.
slides.caption: Three employers hold 51.7% of the city: Axis Bank with 113, EY with 74 and Deloitte with 47. JP Morgan Chase adds 34 and Morgan Stanley 29.
Bengaluru holds 24.8%, which is 512 roles, more than Mumbai. NCR holds 17.9%, which is 371 roles from 32 employers. Hyderabad holds 11.1% from 28 employers. Pune holds 6.6%.

slides.lead: More roles, twice as many doors.
slides.text: 65 employers at 7.9 roles each. The most-named skill is SQL, ahead of financial services and Python.
slides.caption: Bengaluru holds 24.8%, which is 512 roles, more than Mumbai. They come from 65 employers at 7.9 each. Bengaluru's most-named skill is SQL (81), ahead of financial services (80), regulatory requirements (69), regulatory compliance (69), Python (61) and financial statements (56). A finance job in Bengaluru is a finance job run as analytics.

slides.lead: Delhi NCR is one firm's market.
slides.text: EY posts 39.6% of every finance opening there. Pune is 63.0% senior and above. Hyderabad's entry level is 8.0%.
slides.caption:
EY posts 147 of them, 39.6% of every finance opening in the metro. Pune holds 6.6% and is 63.0% senior and above, the most experienced finance market in India. Entry level is 8.0%, the lowest of the big metros.
